summary.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12.3% to ₹570.9 crore and EBITDA margin expanded ~250 bps to 22.9%, with a PAT of ₹95.8 crore (+24.8%).
summary.overview: Management framed FY26 as a shift toward value-added components, assemblies and OEM/Tier-1 engagement, with consolidated EBITDA up 26.0% to ₹130.7 crore. Standalone revenue grew on broadly flat volumes, which management attributed to better realisation (shunt component mix moving from ~55% to ~65%, ~10-12% realisation uplift). Contacts (silver-based) grew sharply, but management said only about 30-31% of the ~54-60% growth was underlying volume, with the rest from silver price pass-through. Management guided to a multi-year re-acceleration led by a US shunt customer's component recovery and a new Pune PCBA/busbar facility targeting ₹250-350 crore revenue over 2-3 years.

financial_highlights.value: not stated as a figure; management cited 329 bps QoQ improvement

segments.name: Shunts
segments.commentary: Shifting from strip to engineered components; component share rising from ~55% to ~65%, yielding ~10-12% higher per-kg realisation. Smart-meter shunt revenue ~₹70 crore odd. India driven by automotive, smart metering, current sensing, BMS and energy management.

segments.name: Electric Contacts (silver-based)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~54-60% in FY26, of which management said ~30-31% is underlying growth and ~21-22% is silver price pass-through. Now a 100% subsidiary (formerly JV until 2023); new plant partially ready for 7-8 months.

segments.name: Thermostatic Bimetals
segments.commentary: India demand flat as domestic consumption has not grown; Europe showed strong traction. Market share in India reportedly ~90%; management is pursuing high-volume export orders, potentially at 1-2% margin sacrifice.

segments.name: PCBA / Busbar (Pune facility)
segments.commentary: Phase one nearly complete; EB-welded CCS/busbars initially for two-wheeler EV, targeting ₹250-350 crore revenue over 2-3 years (management preferred 3 years as safer).

guidance_outlook: US shunt customer: management expects volumes to return to near prior peak levels in FY27 and surpass them in FY27-28; timing could slip by 4-6 quarters.
Customer concentration: top US customer fell from ~38-39% at peak to ~13-14%; expected to rise back to ~16-18% at most.
Smart meters: management expects revenue to roughly double again in FY27; growth visibility for 6-8 quarters, with 4-quarter downside case if installations fall below half of plan.
Medium-term: internal target of 20%+ growth in the near term and closer to 30% if all goes well; aim to return to 30-plus% growth over 5 years.
Capex: no substantial growth capex required; maintenance and automation capex of ₹10-15 crore per year. Consolidated capacity cited at ~₹1,300 crore revenue potential vs ₹570.9 crore today.
Capacity utilisation: ~60% on average currently; management expects ~75-80% in the next two years without major incremental capex.
capex_capacity: Pune facility being set up in phases; phase one almost complete, including R&D centre; targeted at PCBA and EB-welded busbar/CCS assemblies for two-wheeler EV, later hybrid, ICE, BESS and non-automotive current sensing.
Consolidated capacity cited at ~₹1,300 crore revenue potential; utilisation ~43-45% on that basis, but ~60% on management's operational view.
Thermostatic bimetal capacity already fully added; minimal incremental capex needed in that vertical.
Contacts: new plant partly ready for 7-8 months; capacity additions in areas where constraints existed; growth expected to continue FY27.
Rising inventory days linked to copper procurement for the PCBA business and to securing order-backed supply amid geopolitical uncertainty.
demand_pricing: India bimetal demand flat; management linked this to a flat switchgear/MCB market and weak mid-to-low-cost real estate.
US shunt customer revival: product shift from strip to component form; tariffs accelerated direct supply of finished resistors to customer's customers (70-80% outside the US).
Management said it is pursuing high-volume bulk bimetal orders possibly at 1-2% lower margin to fill spare capacity.
Competitor EMS (Texas Instruments legacy, now under a German parent) is shifting capacity away from thermostatic bimetal, creating share opportunity in Europe/US.
Contacts: transparent silver pricing cited as competitive advantage; low-margin, large addressable market.
Working capital: trade receivable days up on export mix; India realisation ~70-75 days, exports 90+ days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realisation uplift per kg in shunts and how much of contacts growth is silver-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Component share rose from ~55% to ~65%, yielding ~10-12% higher per-kg realisation. Management said ~half or a little less of contacts growth was silver price, with underlying business growth ~30-31%.

qa_highlights.question: What is smart meter revenue and FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Smart-meter revenue nearly doubled to over ₹75-80 crore in FY26 from ~₹30-40 crore. Management expects a similar or doubled level in FY27 and 6-8 quarters of growth, with downside scenario of 4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US shunt customer recovery real and what is the timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects volumes to return to near prior peak in FY27 and surpass them in FY27-28, with timing possibly shifting by 4-6 quarters. Business now primarily component-based, with better value add versus strip.

qa_highlights.question: Why was growth muted over the last few years and is FY26's 12% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: The large US customer's sharp decline (over-inventorisation, US market, design changes, competitor shift) masked new business. With that customer no longer dominant, management expects growth at a different level from FY26 onward.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PCBA/busbar revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees ₹250-350 crore revenue from the standalone unit over 2-3 years, starting with two-wheeler EV CCS/busbars, with EB-welded products carrying better margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for growth capex and what is utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: No substantial growth capex; maintenance and automation capex ₹10-15 crore per year. Average utilisation about 60% today, expected 75-80% in two years without major capex.

risks_watch: Contacts growth partly silver price pass-through (~21-22% of growth in management's split); reversal risk if silver falls.
Smart meter installation pace is outside management's control; plateau if implementation falls below half of plan.
US customer forecast timing could slip 4-6 quarters; concentration to rise back to 16-18%.
Rising inventory days and receivable days (export 90+ days, India 70-75 days) affect working capital and cash conversion.
India bimetal demand flat; reliance on export wins and possible 1-2% margin dilution from bulk orders.
Pune PCBA/busbar ramp (₹250-350 crore) depends on customer development timelines that could slip 2-3 years; competition may eventually enter EB welding.
Disclosure gaps: smart meter revenue split between shunts and contacts not fully given; FY26 gross margin figure not stated on a consolidated basis.
summary.management_tone: Confident and strategic on the long-term story and US customer recovery, but guarded on specifics (NDA limits, timing caveats, smart meter dependence). Evasive on some numbers such as contacts volume split and smart meter contribution to revenue, and a few answers needed clarification during Q&A.

we consider any growth coming from smart meters good, or bad,- we consider it to be more of a bonus for us

adds.what: New Pune PCBA/busbar facility (phase one, incl. R&D centre), EB-welded CCS/busbars for two-wheeler EV
Contacts (silver-based) new plant, partly ready, capacity additions in constrained areas

growth.why: Management targets upwards of 20% growth (closer to 30%) with the US shunt customer returning to peak in FY27, smart-meter revenue expected to double in FY27, and the Pune PCBA/busbar unit targeting ₹250-350 crore over 2-3 years; utilisation is ~60% with 75-80% expected in two years without major capex, but the Pune unit's ramp is still unproven and quarterly results were not separately stated.
